title: Poisons, Small Pupils, and a Long-Bone Clue

questions.stem: A shared heater, headache, and a normal oxygen pressure. What is occupying the hemoglobin?

options.text: Nothing; reassure and send home
Carbon monoxide
A nitrate
Fat from a long bone, in the first ten minutes

questions.explanation: The pulse oximeter cannot tell carbon monoxide from oxygen. Check everyone who shared the air.

questions.stem: Small pupils and a breath that has stopped. First move?

options.text: Wait for a line, then a reversal
Support breathing now
Give flumazenil first
Send them home once they blink

questions.explanation: Naloxone follows, and you watch, because it can wear off.

questions.stem: Flumazenil in a daily benzodiazepine user can:

options.text: Only wake them safely, always
Provoke a seizure
Replace support of the airway
Treat fat embolism

questions.stem: Hypoxia, a petechial rash, and confusion a day or two after a long-bone fracture:

options.text: Fat embolism
A simple clot you treat with a thinner as the first and only move
Carbon monoxide from a heater in every case
Pemphigus

questions.explanation: Support the lungs. This is not a clot you treat with a thinner first.

options.text: Keep the trigger on and wait
Stop the trigger and give dantrolene
Treat it as the rigid syndrome after an antipsychotic
Give flumazenil

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide often rises first. The temperature follows.

questions.stem: In carbon monoxide poisoning, the oxygen pressure in arterial blood can:

options.text: Look normal and still not reassure you
Always be very low, so a normal value excludes it
Replace a history of a shared heater
Be read accurately by an ordinary pulse oximeter

questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry cannot tell the two species apart.

options.text: Can be discharged the moment the eyes open
Needs a watch, because depression can return
Should be treated with flumazenil next
Never recurs

questions.stem: A benzodiazepine alone, compared with an opioid:

options.text: More often stops the breath as the first picture
Rarely stops the breath the way an opioid does
Is reversed first with naloxone in every case
Is treated as fat embolism

questions.explanation: If an opioid may also be present, naloxone is the safer reversal.

questions.stem: The early gas clue in malignant hyperthermia is often:

options.text: A falling carbon dioxide
A rising carbon dioxide
A bird's beak
A mitochondrial antibody
Carbon monoxide can leave the oxygen pressure looking normal.
Support breathing before, or with, naloxone in opioid toxicity.
Flumazenil is routine in every sleepy patient.
Fat embolism comes a day or two after a long-bone fracture.

questions.explanation: Flumazenil can seize a dependent patient and is not routine.
